gen_risks.description: Future flood events could trigger a sharp rise in non‑performing loans, eroding capital adequacy of microfinance providers and limiting lending capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain the Climate Risk Fund as a liquidity buffer and enforce pre‑approved contingency lines to quickly recapitalize affected MFPs.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 9: NPLs surged 25.7% after 2022 floods, capital adequacy fell from 14.9% to 11.7%.

gen_risks.description: The CRF may become under‑capitalized if multiple large flood events occur, limiting its ability to provide contingent liquidity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Periodically review CRF capital adequacy and, if needed, seek additional donor or private‑sector contributions before the end of the project.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1 description: CRF capitalized at US$125 million, limited to flood risk; expansion requires extra capital.

gen_risks.description: Delays in verifying trigger conditions could postpone CRF disbursements, leaving borrowers without timely recovery financing.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish automated data feeds from approved third‑party flood models and set clear SOPs for trigger validation within 48 hours.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 31: Triggers rely on government declaration or portfolio impact thresholds, data provided by third‑party service providers.

gen_risks.description: Non‑compliance with the Trust Deed or Project Operations Manual could jeopardize legal standing and fund release.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct quarterly compliance audits by the SBP’s internal audit unit and obtain prior written consent for any amendment.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal Covenants section: Recipient must ensure Trust Deed and Operations Manual are adhered to and not amended without consent.

gen_risks.description: Selected agricultural technology companies may fail to deliver effective climate‑smart services, reducing the impact of the IAL product.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement performance‑based contracts with ATCs and monitor agronomic outcomes; replace under‑performing ATCs through a second AFIC round.
gen_risks.evidence: Product 1 description: ATCs will be selected via AFIC and must provide agritech services to borrowers.

gen_risks.description: The gender‑targeting requirement (≥55% women beneficiaries) may not be met if loan officers exhibit bias or if women lack collateral.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide gender‑bias training for loan officers, enforce higher borrowing cost penalties for non‑compliance, and monitor gender disbursement ratios monthly.
gen_risks.evidence: Gender section: project will ensure at least 55% of CRF beneficiaries are women, with higher borrowing cost for deviation.

gen_risks.description: Parametric insurance backstop may not be purchased or may provide insufficient coverage, limiting CRF’s ability to absorb extreme shocks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set an annual decision rule in the Oversight Committee to secure insurance coverage meeting predefined loss thresholds.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 30: Decision to secure parametric insurance will be undertaken annually by the CRF Oversight Committee.

gen_risks.description: Reliance on third‑party flood modelling data could result in inaccurate trigger assessments due to data quality issues.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate data validation protocols, use multiple independent models, and conduct back‑testing against historical flood events.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 31: Data for triggers will be provided by third‑party service providers such as flood risk modelling firms.

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic instability (inflation, currency depreciation) may increase loan repayment burdens and affect CRF’s real purchasing power.
gen_risks.mitigation: Index CRF disbursements to local inflation and incorporate exchange‑rate hedging mechanisms for foreign‑currency components.
gen_risks.evidence: Fiscal context: PKR 278.64 = US$1; macroeconomic crisis noted as affecting sector growth since 2019.

gen_risks.description: Changes in Pakistan’s financial regulations (e.g., capital adequacy ratios) could restrict MFPs’ ability to draw on CRF liquidity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain active liaison with SBP and SECP to anticipate regulatory revisions and adapt CRF eligibility criteria accordingly.
gen_risks.evidence: Sectoral context: regulatory framework includes Microfinance Institutions Ordinance and capital adequacy minimum of 15%.

gen_risks.description: Increased loan volumes for agritech may lead to higher fertilizer and pesticide use, causing localized environmental degradation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate environmental safeguards in ATC service contracts, promote integrated pest management, and monitor chemical usage in loan‑linked farms.
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental risks paragraph: clustering of loans may increase fertilizer/pesticide use and ambient air quality impacts.

gen_risks.description: Delays in establishing the CRF trust and opening the pooled accounts could postpone project start‑up and fund availability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set firm milestones for Trust Deed execution and account opening, with penalty clauses for missed deadlines.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal Covenants: Trust Deed must be executed and registered before effectiveness; Disbursement section mentions front‑loading to pooled account.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient private‑sector participation may leave a financing gap despite the project being private‑capital enabling.
gen_risks.mitigation: Launch targeted outreach to commercial banks and impact investors, highlighting de‑risking benefits of the CRF to attract co‑financing.
gen_risks.evidence: Project description: CRF aims to enable private capital; mentions need for additional private funds for expanded coverage.

gen_risks.description: Potential misuse or fraud in CRF fund administration could erode trust and deplete resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement strict internal controls, regular external audits by the Auditor General, and transparent reporting of all CRF transactions.
gen_risks.evidence: Fiduciary section: internal audit by SBP, external audit by Auditor General; pooled accounts with segregated child accounts.

gen_risks.description: Weak monitoring and evaluation may fail to capture beneficiary satisfaction or gender‑disaggregated outcomes, limiting learning.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen M&E by conducting bi‑annual beneficiary surveys, gender‑disaggregated data collection, and independent mid‑term review.
gen_risks.evidence: M&E arrangements: beneficiary satisfaction surveys, gender‑disaggregated indicators listed in results framework.

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk is Substantial. The political context in Pakistan remains fluid. However, there has been significant decline in political uncertainty and associated policy instability in recent months, especially in the backdrop of the general elections. Given that a new government took the helm recently and the fact that policy priorities are still being defined, political risks, in particular in the context of the project, remain substantial.
gt_risks.mitigation: In the implementation stage, the risks will be mitigated through frequent monitoring and oversight.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is High. While fiscal consolidation measures have supported short-term stabilization, macroeconomic risks remain high amid a high debt burden (72 percent of GDP), heavy financial sector exposure to government debt, large external financing needs, weak confidence, and little progress with structural reforms. Significant risks include potential worsening of external conditions, further natural disasters, and a slowdown or reversals in policy adjustment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Risks are partly mitigated by government commitment to implementation of reforms under the ongoing International Monetary Fund program, World Bank support to structural policy reforms in the fiscal and power sectors, strong government commitment to the reforms supported by the operation, and the availability of dedicated World Bank technical assistance to implement key reforms.
